chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated that Ali ibn Anbasa said: No'aym ibn Salih al-Matiri narrated to me that Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) narrated from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The best thing is the gift, and it is the key to needs.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social significance of giving gifts in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) identifies gift-giving (Hadiyyah) as a 'key to needs,' emphasizing its role in strengthening social bonds and facilitating the fulfillment of desires. This concept aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of *Tawassul* through good deeds and social etiquette, where generosity opens doors to both material and spiritual objectives.
